description: Congresswoman Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) is seeking applicants for the Fall 2026 internship program in her Washington, D.C. Office. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. The internship program is intended for current undergraduate students, recent college graduates, and students currently enrolled in graduate school. Internships combine administrative and legislative work. Interns are involved in all aspects of the office including constituent services, correspondence, and legislative research, in addition to providing general staff support. The Washington DC internship program also offers an opportunity for a communications internship. This position will assist the communications team with social media, press conferences, and more. To apply for the communications track, applicants should check the press internship interest box in the program application.
responsibilities: Constituent services
Correspondence
Legislative research
General staff support
Drafting for social media (press intern track)
Compiling daily press clips (press intern track)
Clipping and editing videos (press intern track)
Office administrative tasks (press intern track)
Other tasks as assigned by the Communications team (press intern track)
qualifications: Current undergraduate student, recent college graduate, or student currently enrolled in graduate school
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment
Excellent writing skills
Enthusiastic attitude
how_to_apply: Please go to mejia.house.gov/internships to submit the requested information, including your cover letter and resume. No walk-ins or phone calls.

description: Congressman Mike Levin (CA-49) seeks press intern for his Washington, D.C., office for the Fall 2026 term. This internship provides an opportunity for undergraduate students, graduate students, and recent graduates to learn more about the workings of a Congressional office, the legislative process, and the role of a communications team. Internships last approximately three to four months and are intended to be an educational experience. Internships are offered for either academic credit or a stipend. Internship applicants must be high school graduates. Current students and recent graduates will be given first priority for the internship program. Press interns should have strong social media skills and basic familiarity with graphic design and video editing. Submission of a sample graphic or similar communications work with your application is strongly encouraged. Applicants with strong ties to the 49th District are given preference.
responsibilities: Assisting the Communications Director and Digital Manager/Press Secretary in drafting and editing social media content, digital graphics, and other digital materials
Drafting press releases, newsletters, remarks, and talking points
Compiling daily press clips and maintaining press lists
Answering phones and processing mail
Leading constituents on tours of the Capitol
Working on other administrative and communications-related tasks, as directed
qualifications: Must be a high school graduate
General understanding of the U.S. political system
Value open communication
Eager to grow and bring a can-do attitude
Strong social media skills
Basic familiarity with graphic design and video editing
Submission of a sample graphic or similar communications work strongly encouraged
Applicants with strong ties to the 49th District are given preference
how_to_apply: Email a cover letter, resume, three references, and a brief writing sample all in one PDF file, with the file name including internship class, year, last name, and first name (i.e. Fall2026.Doe.Jane.pdf) to CA49.DCInternships@mail.house.gov by July 23. Specify you are applying for the press internship.
equal_opportunity: This office is an equal opportunity employer; we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, gender identity or expression, or sexual orientation. We deeply value the diversity of our employees and encourage candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply.

description: The DC office of Representative Marilyn Strickland (WA-10) is currently accepting applicants for a paid Fall Communications Internship with a start date of Monday, August 24, 2026, until December 2026, with the potential to extend. This is in addition to answering phones, inputting casework inquiries, and aiding in office needs. Experience working in communications is a plus. Ideal candidates for this internship are diligent, detail-oriented, and can excel in a fast-paced environment. Applicants should possess strong written and verbal communication skills, an eye for and ability to create engaging digital content, and a good sense of humor. Ties to Washington State are preferred, but not required. Applicants are encouraged to include any previous customer service experience (retail, food service, hospitality, etc.) on their resumes. Interested applicants should send a resume, cover letter, a one-page writing sample, and a sample social media post with relevant written and visual components in a single PDF document to WA10resumes@gmail.com with "DC Fall Communications Internship-[LAST NAME]" in the subject line. Please indicate in the cover letter which internship you are applying for and your dates of availability. While the deadline for applications is Wednesday, August 5th at 5PM EST, applications will be accepted and reviewed on a rolling basis. Applicants are encouraged to submit their application early. Applications that are incomplete or submitted after the deadline will not be considered. This office is an Equal Employment Opportunity Office and does not discriminate in employment based on race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, national origin, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, genetic information, age, military service, or other non-merit factors. Individuals from underrepresented communities are encouraged to apply. Please no unsolicited phone calls or drop-ins.

description: The Office of Representative Chrissy Houlahan (D-PA-06) is accepting applications for Fall 2026 legislative interns in our West Chester, Reading, and Washington, D.C. offices. This internship will run from mid-August through mid-December. Both full and part time internships are available, and we offer stipends to applicants, with accommodations for Pell-eligible applicants. Our internship program has returned to in-person work with flexible telework options should interns need to work from home. Ideal applicants are self-starters who bring a customer service mindset and a passion for community service. Applicants must be intellectually curious, willing to spend a lot of time on the phone and write well. Responsibilities range from helping constituents, to doing research and drafting memos for our legislative staff, to staffing the Congresswoman in hearings or meetings. We offer interns the opportunity to see Congress up close and from the inside. Prior volunteer, leadership, and work experience are a plus. Ties to PA-06 are also a plus. Please submit applications through the "Legislative Internship" form our website, Houlahan.house.gov. Due to a high volume of applicants, you will likely only be contacted if you are selected for an interview. This office is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate based on race, religion, disability, age, ethnicity, national origin, sex, gender, LGBTQ identification, family status, or military status. Women, people of color, and other members of traditionally underrepresented communities are strongly encouraged to apply.
